chunks: And Ali ibn al-Husayn informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us in Qum, saying: Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi narrated to us, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Miskan, from Malik ibn A'yun al-Juhani, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far al-Baqir saying:
Every banner that is raised before the rising of al-Qa'im, its owner is a taghut.
ai.seo_question: Who is considered a taghut before the appearance of al-Qa'im?
ai.summary: In the context of the major occultation, this hadith from *Kitab al-Ghayba* serves as a critical criterion for distinguishing legitimate authority from the myriad pretenders who emerge before the Mahdi's return. By classifying all pre-Qa'im banners as 'taghut,' Imam al-Baqir emphasizes that political legitimacy is exclusively reserved for the Awaited Imam, rendering other claimants inherently false and oppressive. This underscores the Shia doctrine of waiting (intizar) not as passive inactivity, but as active discernment of true leadership amidst political chaos.
